executionScopes.title: Local TTS performance + new providers: persistent processes, sidecars, KittenTTS, Kokoro
executionScopes.description:
## Why this exists

Today every PiperTTS.synthesize_stream call spawns a fresh piper subprocess (backend/app/providers/piper_tts.py:693 -> _spawn_process at line 746). The ONNX runtime + voice-model cold-start adds ~200-400 ms of pure overhead PER conversation turn. Unlike Parakeet (where per-request load only hurt the catalog Test button — meeting providers are pre-loaded by load_active_providers), TTS pays this cost on every reply Johnny speaks in a real meeting.

This epic does for TTS what the Parakeet runtime split did for STT:

1. Give the existing Piper provider a runtime picker (subprocess / persistent-subprocess / http-sidecar), defaulting to the safe current behaviour. PRD already written at tasks/prd-piper-tts-runtime-options.md.
2. Add two new local TTS providers (KittenTTS, Kokoro) with the same 3-runtime shape so the user can pick whichever voice + speed trade-off they want.

Each provider exposes the same kind of Runtime dropdown in Settings -> Providers, with structured `<provider>.synth: runtime=... ttfa_ms=...` INFO logs visible in docker logs api so the user can verify the picker is actually doing what they expect and debug runtime-specific failures independently.

## Acceptance for the epic as a whole

- Three providers (Piper, KittenTTS, Kokoro) each ship with three selectable runtimes covering the in-container default, an in-container optimised path, and an out-of-container sidecar option.
- Real meeting hot-path TTS latency drops from ~300 ms cold to <= 100 ms warm on whichever provider the user picks for the in-container optimised path.
- README has a new "Local TTS providers" table listing voices, sample-rate quirks, and the three runtime options per provider.
- Browser-validated via chrome-devtools MCP for each provider: switch runtime in the modal, click Play sample, observe latency badge + structured log.

## Child issues

- Piper runtime split (subprocess / persistent / http-sidecar) — PRD at tasks/prd-piper-tts-runtime-options.md.
- KittenTTS provider (https://github.com/KittenML/KittenTTS) with the same 3-runtime picker.
- Kokoro provider (https://github.com/hexgrad/kokoro) with the same 3-runtime picker.

## Reference implementation

The Parakeet runtime split is the canonical example to copy:
- Module-level cache + per-key asyncio.Lock + global load gate: backend/app/providers/parakeet_stt.py (search for `_LAST`, `_LOAD_LOCKS`, `_GLOBAL_LOAD_GATE`, `_ensure_model`, `evict_process_cache`).
- Runtime dispatch inside transcribe_stream: parakeet_stt.py:_transcribe_in_container vs _transcribe_via_sidecar.
- Sidecar wire protocol + launcher script: sidecars/parakeet-mlx/ and scripts/start-parakeet-sidecar.sh.
- Test seam (autouse fixture evicts the module cache between tests): backend/tests/providers/test_parakeet_stt.py:_reset_parakeet_process_cache.
